questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Simplify sqrt(50).

feedback.text: This does not square back to 50.
The perfect square factor should be rooted.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Rewrite x³⁄⁴ in radical form.

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator 4 is the root index and the numerator 3 is the power.
A rational exponent is not multiplication by 4.
This uses square root instead of fourth root.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Evaluate 27²⁄³.

feedback.text: This does not apply the cube root.
Correct. The cube root of 27 is 3, and 3 squared is 9.
This stops after taking the cube root.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.2

What is the domain of f(x)=sqrt(x+4)?

feedback.text: This allows negative radicands to the left.
Inputs less than -4 are not allowed.
Correct. The radicand must be nonnegative.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.2

What is the range of f(x)=sqrt(x) - 3?

feedback.text: Correct. The square root output starts at 0, then shifts down 3.
The graph shifts down, not up.
A square root graph has a minimum output here.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.1; MLA.A2.RR.3

Solve sqrt(x-2)=4.

feedback.text: This subtracts 2 instead of adding it.
This is the radical value, not x.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.1; MLA.A2.RR.3

Which value checks for sqrt(x+9)=x-3?

feedback.text: Correct. x = 0 appears after squaring but fails the original equation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.1; MLA.A2.RR.3

A model d=sqrt(16t) has d=20. What is t?

feedback.text: This is d squared, not t.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.6

Simplify (x²-9)/(x-3).

feedback.text: Correct. Factor as (x-3)(x+3) and keep the original restriction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.6

What restriction applies to 4/(x+5)?

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator is zero at x=-5.
The numerator does not restrict the domain.
One input makes the denominator zero.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.6

Multiply (2x/3)(9/x²).

feedback.text: One x remains in the denominator.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q12

MLA Standard: Support-only extension of MLA.A2.AE.6; no new primary MLA standard

Simplify 2/x + 5/x.

feedback.text: Correct. Common denominators stay the same while numerators add.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q13

MLA Standard: Support-only extension of MLA.A2.AE.6; no new primary MLA standard

Simplify 1/x + 1/(x+2).

feedback.text: Correct. Use LCD x(x+2) and combine x+2+x.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

Solve 6/x = 3.

feedback.text: Correct. Multiply by x to get 6=3x.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

Solve 2/(x-1)=1.

feedback.text: Correct. Multiply by x-1 to get 2=x-1.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

Which value is restricted in 1/(x-8)=2?

feedback.text: This is not a denominator zero.
The denominator is not zero at 0.
Correct. The denominator x-8 cannot be zero.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

What is the vertical asymptote of f(x)=1/(x+6)?

Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=5/x?

feedback.text: Correct. A constant over x approaches 0 as x grows.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=(2x+1)/(x-4)?

feedback.text: Equal degrees do not approach 0 here.
Correct. Equal degrees use the leading coefficient ratio 2/1.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

In T(n)=90/n, why is n=0 not allowed?

feedback.text: It is not in the domain.

answer.text: division by zero is undefined and zero objects is not meaningful

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator and context both reject n=0.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Simplify sqrt(98).

feedback.text: This does not square back to 98.
The perfect square should be rooted.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Evaluate 16³⁄⁴.

feedback.text: This stops at the fourth root squared incorrectly.
Correct. The fourth root of 16 is 2 and 2³=8.
This cubes 4 instead of the fourth root.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.2

What is the starting point of f(x)=sqrt(x-2)+5?

feedback.text: Correct. The square root starts when x-2=0, then y=5.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.1; MLA.A2.RR.3

Solve sqrt(3x+1)=4.

feedback.text: This does not make the radicand 16.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.6

Simplify (x²+4x)/(x).

feedback.text: Correct. Factor x(x+4) and keep the original restriction.
The common factor x should cancel.
Canceling only one term is invalid.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q26

MLA Standard: Support-only extension of MLA.A2.AE.6; no new primary MLA standard

Simplify 3/(x+1) - 1/(x+1).

feedback.text: Correct. Subtract numerators over the common denominator.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

Solve x/(x-2)=3.

feedback.text: Correct. Multiply by x-2 to get x=3x-6.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

What is the domain of f(x)=(x+1)/(x-7)?

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator is zero at x=7.

Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.1; MLA.A2.RR.3

What makes a radical equation solution extraneous?

feedback.text: Correct. A candidate from squaring must check in the original equation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

What makes a rational equation solution invalid?

answer.text: it makes an original denominator zero

feedback.text: Correct. Restrictions from original denominators must be honored.

answer.text: it was found after clearing denominators

feedback.text: That process is valid if restrictions are checked.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.2

Which parent function has domain x >= 0 and range y >= 0?

feedback.text: A quadratic has all real domain.
A cubic has all real domain and range.
Correct. The square root parent starts at the origin and extends right/up.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.6

Divide (x²-1)/(x+2) by (x-1)/(x+2).

feedback.text: Correct. Multiply by the reciprocal and keep restrictions.
Original denominators and divisor create restrictions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

Which rational function has vertical asymptote x=-3?

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator is zero at x=-3.

Simplify 1/(x-1)+1/(x+1).

Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.AE.7; MLA.A2.AE.8

Rewrite cuberoot(x²) using rational exponents.

feedback.text: Correct. Cube root gives denominator 3 and power 2 gives numerator 2.
The 2 is an exponent, not a coefficient.
The exponents are not multiplied this way.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.5; MLA.A2.RR.6

What does a vertical asymptote represent in a rational model?

answer.text: an input the model approaches but cannot use

feedback.text: Correct. The denominator restriction creates an input where the model is undefined.
An asymptote is not necessarily a maximum.
An x-intercept is where output is 0.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.RR.4

Solve 10/(x+3)=2.

feedback.text: This is not the solved value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U03_UA_Q40

MLA Standard: Unit 3 standards synthesis; no new primary MLA standard

Which check is most important in Unit 3 equation solving?

answer.text: verify candidates in the original equation and restrictions

feedback.text: Correct. Radical and rational equations can create invalid candidates.
